nodes.title: Validate the hex string before parsing it
nodes.why: parseInt silently accepts partial input such as 'ff' from '#ffzz', so the shape has to be checked first.
nodes.alternative: Parse first and check for NaN afterwards.
nodes.tradeoff: One regular expression rejects names, missing # and wrong lengths in a single place.

nodes.title: Expand #abc to #aabbcc
nodes.why: CSS defines each shorthand digit as doubled, so #abc and #aabbcc must give identical results.
nodes.alternative: Scale the single digits by 17 instead of doubling the characters.
nodes.tradeoff: Doubling the characters keeps one parsing path for both forms.

nodes.title: Undo the sRGB curve for each channel
nodes.why: Stored sRGB values are gamma encoded; luminance has to be computed on linear light.
nodes.tradeoff: Skipping the curve is cheaper but gives wrong ratios for every mid tone.

nodes.title: Weight green, red and blue differently
nodes.why: The eye is most sensitive to green and least to blue, which is why pure blue on white still has a high ratio.
nodes.tradeoff: An average is simpler but disagrees with the WCAG definition and every checker.

nodes.title: Divide lighter by darker and keep full precision
nodes.why: Ordering by luminance makes the result symmetric, and the unrounded value keeps 4.48 below the 4.5 threshold.
nodes.alternative: Round to one decimal for display inside the function.
nodes.tradeoff: Rounding belongs in the UI; the comparison needs the raw number.

nodes.title: Precompute the curve for all 256 channel values
nodes.why: A linter that checks hundreds of token pairs repeats the same 256 power calculations; a table does each once.
nodes.alternative: Call Math.pow on every channel of every color.
nodes.tradeoff: 256 numbers of memory for constant-time lookups.

nodes.title: Read the channels with bit shifts
nodes.why: One parseInt over six digits gives a 24-bit integer whose bytes are red, green and blue.
nodes.alternative: Slice the string three times and parse each pair.
nodes.tradeoff: Shifts avoid three substrings per color but are harder to read for juniors.

nodes.title: Sort the two luminances so the lighter comes first
nodes.why: Sorting two numbers descending is a compact way to make the ratio symmetric.
nodes.tradeoff: Same result; max and min avoid allocating an array.

nodes.title: Same formula, cheaper per pair
nodes.why: The output is identical to approach 1, so tests and thresholds do not change.
nodes.alternative: Cache whole colors in a Map keyed by the hex string.
nodes.tradeoff: A per-channel table is bounded at 256 entries; a color cache grows with the palette.
